evals.name: validates-rendered-quiz-policy-without-settings-edits
evals.expected_output: Reports the rendered quiz_policy, report_library_dir, workspace_root and explain_starting_rung (or their defaults), explains quiz offer cadence, runs the setup-apply script's --check for docs/conventions/education.yaml, and never reads or edits settings files or pluginConfigs.
expectations: Reads only the rendered user_config values supplied to the skill
Explains the on-request default and the private plugin-data report fallback
Reports docs/conventions/education.yaml from the script's --check output, as INFO absent when there is no file
Does not inspect or edit settings files or pluginConfigs

evals.name: routes-changes-through-claude-configuration
evals.prompt:
/education:setup

Store quiz reports in a shared corpus checkout.
evals.expected_output: Recommends a portable corpus location, directs the user to Claude Code's plugin configuration prompt for report_library_dir, and requires a rerun before claiming the value changed. It does not write report_library_dir into docs/conventions/education.yaml, which holds no such key.
expectations: Uses repository evidence before recommending a library location
Rejects machine-absolute team paths
Routes persistence through Claude Code and verifies on rerun
Does not write report_library_dir into the repository file

evals.name: refuses-to-edit-settings-for-a-quiz-policy-change
evals.prompt: /education:setup set quiz_policy to always in settings.json for me.
evals.expected_output: Does not edit settings.json or pluginConfigs. It reports the current rendered quiz_policy and routes a persistent change through Claude Code's plugin configuration prompt, then requires a rerun before claiming the value changed.
expectations: Does not write settings.json or pluginConfigs
Routes the persistent change through Claude Code's native configuration prompt
Verifies on a rerun rather than claiming the write succeeded

evals.name: apply-writes-a-fresh-repository-file
evals.prompt:
/education:setup apply explain_starting_rung=peer

[The repository has no docs/conventions/education.yaml yet.]
evals.expected_output: Runs check first, then calls the setup-apply script with explain_starting_rung=peer. The script creates docs/conventions/education.yaml holding explain_starting_rung: peer and no other key. The re-run check reports the value from the file, and the tracked-file pair reports the file as written but untracked, telling the operator to commit it so the team receives it. No other file is written.
expectations: Runs check before writing
Writes only docs/conventions/education.yaml, holding explain_starting_rung: peer and no other key
Reports the value from the re-run check, not from the write alone
Says the new file is untracked and must be committed to reach the team, rather than reporting plain success
Does not edit settings files, pluginConfigs or .gitignore

evals.name: apply-shows-the-diff-before-changing-an-existing-file
evals.prompt:
/education:setup apply explain_starting_rung=plain

[docs/conventions/education.yaml already exists and holds explain_starting_rung: peer under a comment line.]
evals.expected_output: The first script call exits 3 and prints a unified diff from explain_starting_rung: peer to explain_starting_rung: plain without writing. The skill shows that diff, asks the operator whether to write it, and stops for the answer. It re-runs with --yes only after an explicit yes; the comment line stays in the file.
expectations: Shows the diff from peer to plain before anything is written
Asks for confirmation and does not pass --yes in the same turn as showing the diff
Does not treat the original apply request as confirmation of the diff
Leaves the file unchanged when the operator has not said yes

evals.name: apply-refuses-an-invalid-value
evals.expected_output: The script refuses explain_starting_rung=expert because it is not plain or peer, exits 1 and writes nothing. The skill reports the key, the rejected value and the two allowed values, and offers to write one of them instead; it does not write expert by hand or create the file another way.
expectations: Names explain_starting_rung, the rejected value expert, and the allowed values plain and peer
Writes no file, by the script or by hand
Offers a valid value instead of persisting the invalid one

evals.name: check-warns-on-a-duplicate-key
evals.prompt:
/education:setup check

[docs/conventions/education.yaml sets explain_starting_rung twice, first plain, then peer.]
evals.expected_output: Check reports a WARN row quoting the file and saying explain_starting_rung is set twice, from the script's --check output, and says /education:explain drops that layer rather than stopping. It writes nothing and says one of the two lines must be removed by hand, since apply refuses a file that sets a key twice.
expectations: Reports the duplicate key as a WARN naming docs/conventions/education.yaml and explain_starting_rung
Does not report either plain or peer as the repository value
Writes nothing during check
